lines.trans: I'll sell these.
They won't sell that easily.
You're interesting. I'll buy them from you.
Thank you very much. As expected of the owner, you have a keen eye!
They sold! Three thousand yen each, that's sixty thousand yen.
Were you a salesman or something?!
That's right. About how many of these sell in a day?
Well, two a day at most.
Then let's hit other shops too. Our daily target is sixty.
Hold on a second. You mean teaming up with me?
Is that a problem?
Are you prepared to enter this world?
They won't sell that easily.

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Casual, blunt contraction of あなた used between intimates or in heated speech.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Attaches to quantities or interrogatives (どのぐらい, 何本ぐらい) to indicate approximation.

examples.text: 一日何本ぐらい売れる？
examples.trans: About how many sell in a day?

examples.text: 十分ぐらい待ちました。

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.en: as one would expect; true to reputation
meanings.note: Expresses admiration when someone lives up to their reputation.

examples.text: さすがオーナー様、お目が高い！
examples.trans: As expected of the owner, you have a keen eye!
You're a pro, just as expected.

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
na-adjective.
Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Loanword from English 'owner', commonly used for shop or bar owners.
Read いちにち for duration/rate ('per day'); read ついたち for the 1st of the month.

examples.text: 一日十五分勉強します。
examples.trans: I study for fifteen minutes a day.

meanings.note: Number 一 + counter 本 (with sound change to いっぽん).

examples.text: ペンを一本貸してください。

meanings.note: Combines 三千 (3,000) with 円 (yen).

examples.text: 三千円お預かりします。

meanings.note: Used for the physical world or a specific sphere/industry (この世界).

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるか。
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Number 二 + counter 本.
Often used with の (他の店) to mean 'other shops'.

examples.trans: Let's go to other shops too.

examples.text: 他に質問はありますか。
examples.trans: Do you have any other questions?

meanings.note: Polite volitional 会いましょう in また会いましょう means 'let us meet again'.

examples.trans: I meet a friend at the station.

examples.text: また来週会いましょう。

meanings.note: Interrogative 何 + counter 本.

examples.text: 一日何本ぐらい売れてるんだ？
examples.trans: About how many sell in a day?

examples.text: ビールは何本ありますか。
examples.trans: How many bottles of beer are there?

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Godan verb: potential polite 入れます (はいれます) means 'can enter'.

examples.text: 予約なしでも入れますか。
examples.trans: Can we get in without a reservation?

meanings.note: Number 六万 + currency counter 円.

examples.trans: It's sixty thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Number 六十 + counter 本 (with sound change to ろくじゅっぽん).

examples.text: 一日の目標は六十本だ。

meanings.note: Compound of 営業 (sales/business) + マン (man).

examples.text: あんた営業マンだったのかよ？
examples.trans: Were you a salesman or something?!

meanings.note: て-form 売って links 'sell' into the next action.
Intransitive verb describing goods selling on the market without naming a seller.

examples.text: この絵本はよく売れます。
新しい本がたくさん売れました。
examples.trans: Many copies of the new book sold.

meanings.note: I-adjective; 多くて means 'at most'.

examples.text: 今日は人が多いですね。
examples.trans: There are a lot of people today.

meanings.note: Core noun for any retail shop or café; often takes polite お to become お店.

examples.trans: There is a shop in front of the station.

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.
More formal than さん, standard when addressing customers (お客様, お二人様).

examples.text: お客様、こちらへどうぞ。

meanings.note: Noun.
A specific quantitative or concrete aim.

examples.text: 一日の目標は六十本だ。

meanings.note: Na-adjective; 簡単に means 'easily'.

examples.text: そう簡単に売れないよ。

meanings.en: to team up; to partner with; to cross (arms/legs)
meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.text: 彼と組むことになった。
examples.trans: I ended up teaming up with him.

meanings.note: Mental readiness to face something difficult or risky.

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるのか？
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: 買えます is the polite potential form meaning 'can buy / can afford to buy'.

examples.text: 本屋で雑誌を買いました。
examples.trans: I bought a magazine at the bookstore.

examples.text: この値段なら買えますよ。
examples.trans: At this price, we can buy it.

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: この映画はとても面白いです。
何か面白い話はありませんか。
examples.trans: Do you have any interesting stories?

meanings.note: I-adjective meaning expensive (price) or high/tall.

examples.text: この時計はとても高いです。
少し高いと感じるかもしれません。
examples.trans: You may feel it's a little expensive.
